A write-ahead log is a record of all changes made to a database, including inserts, updates, and deletes. This log is maintained independently of the database itself, meaning that the log is not stored within the database files. When a transaction is committed, the changes to the database are written to the log before they are written to the database. This ensures that there is an up-to-date record of all changes, even if the database itself becomes corrupted or unavailable.
If a crash occurs, the database can recover by replaying the transactions recorded in the write-ahead log. This is done by reapplying the changes to the database, starting with the most recent transactions and working backwards. Any changes that are still in the log but have not yet been written to the database will be reapplied, while any changes that were partially written to the database will be discarded. This ensures that the database is left in a consistent state, even if the crash occurred while a transaction was in progress.
